fault_notes: The agent makes no meaningful diagnostic enquiries into Kofi's broadband speeds and offers only generic advice, without properly investigating the connection. The agent repeatedly deflects responsibility, suggesting the issue is caused by Kofi's devices or home setup and that an independent technician or the router manufacturer should handle it, rather than taking ownership of the broadband service complaint. [On saving, four unlisted faults added: noname (the agent never says "Kofi" or "Mensah"); empathy (the customer falls to -74 and the agent only says "I appreciate that you're unhappy. However..." before deflecting again); rapport (dismissive lines: "Whether you choose to follow them is up to you", "That's your choice"); noconfirm (nothing is fixed or checked; the customer ends with "nothing has actually been checked"). Not added: nopara, although the agent hardly restates the problem; this call is already overloaded.]

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you for calling S-Net. You're speaking with Hannah. How can I help you today?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Hi Hannah. It's Kofi. I'm calling because my broadband is nowhere near the speed I was promised when I signed up. It's been really disappointing.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Right, I can give you some general advice about broadband speeds. First, have you tried restarting your router?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: I've restarted it several times already. I'm paying for a package that was supposed to be much faster than this.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Okay. Routers can sometimes behave unpredictably. You could try turning it off for thirty seconds and switching it back on.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: I've literally just said I've restarted it several times. It doesn't make any difference. Can you check the speed I'm supposed to be getting?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I can explain the package information, but actual speeds can depend on things within your home, so you may need to look at your own equipment.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: But the broadband comes from S-Net. The package was advertised at one hundred megabits, and I'm not getting anything close to that.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: The advertised speed is generally an estimate of what may be achievable. You can check your router manual for more information.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: I understand speeds can vary, but this is consistently slow. Even basic video calls keep freezing. I need someone to actually look into it.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I see. Before we continue, I'll just need to verify your account. Can you provide the security answer registered on your account?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: It's Accra.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you. That's verified. I'll open your account now.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Thanks. I really don't want another generic checklist. I've already spent time restarting things and checking cables.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Well, those are the usual things customers can do themselves. If you've completed them, the next step is probably checking the device you're using.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: It's not just one device. My laptop and my phone both seem slow when they're connected to the Wi-Fi. Surely that suggests something with the connection.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Different devices can have different wireless capabilities. You could contact the laptop manufacturer or your phone support team for advice.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: I've noticed it on both devices, and both worked fine at my previous address. I don't see why I should contact two manufacturers about my broadband.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I understand, but we can't guarantee the performance of equipment connected to the router. You might want to consider upgrading your router.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: The router was supplied by S-Net with this package. Why would I have to buy another one when I'm already paying you every month?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: The supplied router is provided as part of the service, but the environment it's used in can affect performance. You could move it somewhere more central.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: It's already in the living room, in the open, and I'm sitting right next to it when I test. I'm not sure what else you want me to do.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: You could try changing the Wi-Fi channel. There should be instructions in the router settings or manual.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: I don't know how to do that, and I don't think I should have to become a network engineer just to get the service I signed up for.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: There are online guides that can walk you through it. Alternatively, an independent technician could inspect your home network.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: An independent technician would cost me extra. I'm asking S-Net to check whether I'm getting the broadband speed you're charging me for.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: We can provide the package details, but the speed you experience is affected by many things outside our control. That's why local equipment checks are recommended.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Can you at least tell me what speed the line is currently delivering? Surely you have a way to check that from your side.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I'm not able to provide a precise measurement from this screen. You could run a speed test on one of the public websites.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: I've done speed tests already. They show around twelve to fifteen megabits, which is nowhere near the advertised hundred. That's why I'm calling.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Speed tests can be affected by the testing website and the device. I'd suggest trying a different website and comparing the results.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: I've tried more than one website. The results are similar every time. I don't think repeating the test is going to solve anything.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: If the results are consistent, that may point to a limitation in your home setup. You could ask a technician to review the wiring and devices.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: You're sending me in circles. I've told you the router is in the open, I've restarted it, and I've tested multiple devices. What is S-Net actually going to do?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: At this stage, I can only suggest the standard troubleshooting steps. Anything beyond those may require assistance from an equipment specialist.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: That's not acceptable. I bought the package because I need a reliable connection for work, and the service hasn't been close to what was promised.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I appreciate that you're unhappy. However, we can't be responsible for every factor that affects your connection inside the property.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: I'm not asking you to be responsible for everything in my house. I'm asking you to check your service before blaming things that you've not even inspected.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: You may be able to arrange a technician through a local computer shop. They can assess whether the router or your internal wiring is causing the slowdown.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: So I'm supposed to pay someone else to diagnose a problem with a service I'm already paying S-Net for? That doesn't seem fair.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I can only explain the options available to you. An independent assessment would help determine whether the issue is with your own setup.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Can you check for an outage or a known problem in my area? That's a simple thing you should be able to do.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Service interruptions are usually posted on our website. You can check the service status page using your postcode.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: I called because I thought you could check that for me. Why am I being told to go online and do everything myself?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: The status page is the most convenient way to see general notices. I don't have any further information to add from here.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: I don't understand how a support call can end with no actual check, no explanation, and no next step from the company.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I've given you the troubleshooting options available. If you need a more detailed inspection, you'll need to arrange it independently.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: I want this escalated. I'm not happy with the service, and I'm certainly not happy with being told to spend more money to investigate it.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Escalation may not change the outcome if the cause is related to your internal equipment. You would be better off getting that checked first.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: But you haven't established that it's my equipment. You've just assumed it is. Can you please log a complaint about this call?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I can record that you're dissatisfied with the advice. For a formal complaint, you can use the complaints section of our website.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: You're not even willing to take ownership of the problem. I've explained everything, and I still don't have an answer or a plan.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I have explained the steps that are available to you. Whether you choose to follow them is up to you.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: That's exactly the problem. I'm asking for support, not a list of things to do on my own. I expected better from S-Net.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I understand your position, but we can't diagnose every customer's home network over the phone. An independent technician is the practical option.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Fine, I'll consider making a complaint. I still don't have the speed I signed up for, and this call hasn't helped.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: That's your choice. You can find the relevant contact details on our website if you decide to proceed.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Before we finish, is there anything at all you can do from your side? Even a basic line check or a service report?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I don't have a line diagnostic available in this call view. The router manual and an independent technician are still the options I'd suggest.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Right. So nothing has actually been checked, and I'm still stuck with the same slow connection.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I've shared the available suggestions. If you need further assistance with your home equipment, please contact a specialist. Thank you for choosing S-Net.
